To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
employee share ownership does not seem to have a positive impact on firm performance.
the presence of employees in the control bodies is not correlated with the performance of the companies.
the presence of employee-shareholders in the board of director or in the board of trustees is associated with lower performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of the role of employee shareholders in corporate governance.
the role played by employee shareholders in the corporate governance of French companies.
the role of employee ownership in corporate governance, which is still an open question.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no evidence of a positive impact of employee ownership on corporate value creation.
employee shareholders have a negative effect on corporate governance and performance.
the employee shareholders do not have a positive impact on the performance of the companies in which they are shareholders.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
employee ownership is not a substitute for the market for corporate control.
employee ownership has a negative impact on firm value, but this impact may be positive in the presence of a strong employee participation.
the presence of employees in the governance structure does not have a positive influence on performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
employee-shareholders are not necessarily a positive element for the corporate governance of companies.
employee ownership does not necessarily lead to better governance.
the presence of employee-shareholders in the control bodies of French firms is associated with lower performance.
